title: NIA Exposes Pakistan's 'Doctor-Terror' Module in Ghazwa-e-Hind Plot
excerpt: India's National Investigation Agency has exposed what it describes as Pakistan's plan to advance the concept of 'GhazwaeHind'—an ideological call for the conquest of India—through a newly uncovered 'doctorterror' mod…
body:
India's National Investigation Agency has exposed what it describes as Pakistan's plan to advance the concept of 'Ghazwa-e-Hind'—an ideological call for the conquest of India—through a newly uncovered 'doctor-terror' module. According to the NIA's findings, the network recruited medical professionals to serve as sleeper agents, leveraging their social standing and mobility to operate beneath the radar of conventional intelligence surveillance.

The agency's disclosures come as part of an ongoing investigation into cross-border terror financing and radicalisation pipelines. Officials say the module was designed to exploit professional visa pathways and educational exchanges to embed operatives in Indian institutions, a tactic that marks a departure from traditional infiltration methods along the Line of Control.

The revelation carries particular resonance for the Indian diaspora, many of whom maintain professional and family ties that span the subcontinent's borders. Security analysts note that the 'doctor-terror' concept mirrors tactics seen in other geographies where professionals have been recruited for extremist purposes, including the 2007 Glasgow airport attack carried out by medical practitioners.

India's Ministry of External Affairs has not yet issued a formal response, but the NIA's findings are likely to intensify diplomatic pressure on Pakistan ahead of upcoming bilateral engagements.
author: Diaspora Desk
